_about: The load file for the two pilot documents (#2498, design v3 section 5): each row is a draft observation matched to an existing observation (enrich) or none (add). Built from the two draft JSONs and the processing plan; applied by iba/app/lib/draftapply.py. Nothing in this file is written until the researcher approves the rehearsal.

rows.obs_text: Those who were far off are described by what they lack, hope and God; their nearness is brought about for them (hostility put to death, peace preached to far and near) and is not something they reach. Read: two distances, to God and to one another, are closed by the same act.
People seek God and grope toward him, yet he is near each of them: the seeking is directed at one who is already close.
One recognition, spoken by one disciple, is met in different ways: Peter hears it and throws himself into the sea, the others come in the boat with the net. Read: none of the responses is corrected.

The son rehearses a request to be treated as a hired servant because he is no longer worthy, but the father, seeing him still far off, is moved with compassion and runs to him; the servant request is never spoken. Read: the son's rating of himself is set aside, not argued with.
The elders reckon the centurion worthy because he loves their nation; he reckons himself unworthy and says he did not presume to come; Jesus marvels at him.
Paul, asked whether he can persuade in a short time, wishes that all who hear him, in a short or a long time, might become as he is, except for his chains.
The hearers listen to Paul until a particular word, the one that sends him to the Gentiles, and their hearing ends there in a cry for his death.

The Preacher sought words of delight; the words of the wise are likened to goads and to fixed nails, given by one Shepherd. Read: the two figures are two works on the hearer, one that moves and one that fixes.
Those who devour widows' houses make long prayers for a pretense, and are set beside a poor widow who says nothing and puts in all she has, against the many who give from abundance.
Money and a story are given to cover what the guards told, and the carriers of the lie are promised safety from trouble.
Paul wants his hearers free from anxieties, and sets beside it the unmarried man's care for the things of the Lord and how to please him.

rows.draft: FE-50
rows.obs_text: Dread and trembling arise before God himself: before his presence, his voice in the thunder, his word and his acts. Job is terrified at his presence and could not face his majesty; the camp at Sinai trembles; Daniel's companions flee and Daniel is left trembling; Joseph's brothers turn to one another in fear at what God has done; sinners in Zion ask who can live beside the consuming fire.

rows.draft: FE-56
rows.obs_text: Trembling comes at an arrival or a discovery: elders and a priest come trembling to meet Samuel and David, Adonijah's guests rise and scatter, Isaac trembles on learning who brought the game, a man in the night is startled, a people follows in trembling, and towns flee before an advancing army.

rows.draft: FE-63
rows.obs_text: God lays dread on whole peoples, and the verses give what follows: no one can stand against Israel, the kingdoms make no war against Jehoshaphat, the peoples are still as a stone, Egypt is glad when Israel leaves, kings who see Zion are seized with trembling, and the prayer is that the nations tremble at his presence.

rows.draft: FE-67
rows.obs_text: Fear is also done to others as an act, with the one who frightens as the subject: Ahithophel's plan to throw the king's company into a panic, Gideon throwing an army into panic, sorceries from which Babylon hopes to inspire terror, God's justice so that man may strike terror no more, creditors roused to make the debtor tremble, Job asking whether God will frighten a driven leaf, those sent to terrify the nations.

rows.draft: FE-70
rows.obs_text: 'Do not be in dread' is spoken with its ground beside it: the Lord is in their midst, goes with them, or has said it from of old. The same word is turned to oneself as trust: I will not be afraid, whom shall I fear.

rows.draft: FE-72
rows.obs_text: 'None shall make you afraid' is the promise of peace: lying down in the land, sitting under the vine and fig tree, dwelling securely, returning in quiet, being led in safety; Zophar offers it to Job as the outcome of turning.

rows.draft: FE-78
rows.obs_text: The dread root appears in joy: the heart thrills and exults, and the people are struck with awe and trembling at the good and the prosperity provided for them once their guilt is forgiven, beside rejoicing with trembling.

rows.draft: FE-79
rows.obs_text: Trembling is called for and decreed: the earth is told to tremble before the Lord in his holiness, the peoples at his reign, the inhabitants of the land at the coming day; the women at ease are told to shudder; Darius decrees that all tremble before the God of Daniel; the heavens are told to be appalled.

rows.draft: FE-80
rows.obs_text: The physical world and the dead tremble before God, with the words used of people: mountains quake at his anger, the deep trembles when the waters see him, the pillars of heaven tremble at his rebuke, the dead tremble under the waters, and the land trembles at those who trample the needy.

rows.draft: FE-81
rows.obs_text: One Hebrew root, ragaz, 'to tremble', is rendered in the ESV as trembling, anger, raging, quarrelling, grief and disturbance: peoples and earth tremble, the psalmist is told to be angry and not sin, Sennacherib is said to have raged against God, Joseph tells his brothers not to quarrel, David is deeply moved at Absalom's death, Samuel is disturbed at being brought up, Sheol is stirred up.
